items.t: Every first-page card is labelled with the board sub-area "Dewdney Deroche" and a "Mission" mailing address, on streets including Lougheed Highway, Taylor Road, Bergen Road, Cooper Road and Ridgeview Road.

What the page covers — IDENTITY CALL: the two rural communities of Dewdney and Deroche along the Lougheed Highway (Highway 7) corridor east of Mission. It does not cover land inside the City of Mission, despite the "Mission" mailing addresses and the page title's "Mission BC" wording.

Board geography: in the board data, "Dewdney Deroche" is one of nine sub-areas of the Fraser Valley board community "Mission" — a reporting grouping only; it does not make Dewdney or Deroche part of the City of Mission.

Ministry-listed names only are used. School-district coverage (SD75) and municipal governance are different things — SD75 serves these FVRD communities even though the City of Mission does not govern them, and Area G voters elect an SD75 rural trustee. Catchments: no SD75 catchment document or locator run for an address here is on record, so catchment schools for any specific address are UNVERIFIED.

Servicing frame: FVRD bylaws provide for a Deroche water system and an Electoral Area G Dewdney Community Water System — servicing runs through FVRD systems where a lot is inside a service area, not through the City of Mission. Whether a specific lot is on a community system, a private well, or a community sewer vs septic: UNVERIFIED at parcel level.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Dewdney-Deroche

items.t: Form B diligence — stated with its limit: Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. It has no application to the fee-simple acreages and pad-rent manufactured homes that make up this corridor's stock — there is no verified strata building here for it to attach to. If a listing in this corridor ever presents as strata, the Form B is the first document to demand, precisely because no strata stock is verified here.

Rental and age bylaws (strata law, for contrast): strata rental-restriction bylaws have been VOID since Nov 24, 2022 anywhere in BC, and only 55+ residency bylaws are lawful in a strata (Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2 + Regulation 7.01, exemptions expanded May 1, 2023). Neither rule governs a manufactured-home park: a park's age rule and rental position are park-tenancy matters under the park's own documents and the Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act, not strata bylaws — do not read Oasis's "adult side" through strata law, and do not import a directory "rentals not allowed" line into a park purchase.

Fee-simple position — the corridor's actual default: A fee-simple purchase here carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees; FVRD zoning, registered covenants and provincial rural rules govern instead. The corridor's houses and acreages are that product.

Planning and zoning (local): FVRD official community plan and zoning bylaws govern this Electoral Area G ground. Confirm a parcel's designation and zone with the FVRD for the PID. Mission's OCP 6405-2026 does NOT apply here — that is City of Mission ground, west of this corridor.

Rural property taxes — the regime that actually applies: a property not located in a city, town, district or village is in a rural area; its owner receives the property tax notice from the Province's Surveyor of Taxes Office and pays property taxes to the Province, not to the FVRD or the City of Mission. Under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act, s. 11, rural property taxes are due July 2, a 5% penalty is added to any portion that remains unpaid on July 2, and a further 5% penalty is added to any portion that remains unpaid on October 31. Mission's flat 10% penalty is expressly DISAPPLIED here — it is a City of Mission rule for city ground, and Dewdney-Deroche is not city ground; Chilliwack's August second-stage date does not apply here either.

ALR housing rules: parcel-level ALR status is per PID: UNVERIFIED — check the parcel on the Agricultural Land Commission mapping. Where land is in the ALR: generally one principal residence capped at 500 m² total floor area, plus at most one additional residence up to 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha); and ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)).

The process is what is documented: zoning, permits and servicing questions for a parcel go to the FVRD as the local government for Electoral Area G, confirmed per PID before any build, subdivision or second-dwelling plan is priced.

Subdivision / servicing — process documented, no bylaw number asserted: no FVRD subdivision-servicing bylaw number is verified for this ground (UNVERIFIED, above), so the documented position is procedural: subdivision of a Dewdney-Deroche parcel runs through the FVRD/provincial approving process for electoral-area ground, with servicing proven parcel by parcel — community water where the lot is inside an FVRD service area (Deroche water system; Electoral Area G Dewdney Community Water System), otherwise private well and septic, each UNVERIFIED at parcel level until the specific lot's service-area position is confirmed with the FVRD.

Flood diligence — the corridor's defining land check: the FVRD has issued freshet evacuation alerts for Area G ground including Nicomen Island and the Taylor Road area in Deroche, and the lowland parts of this corridor are Fraser River floodplain ground.

ALR block (provincial frame, for the corridor's farmland parcels): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).
Second dwellings on non-ALR ground: Confirm with the FVRD per PID.

Rural property taxes — the jurisdiction rule in full: a property not located in a city, town, district or village is in a rural area; its owner receives the property tax notice from the Province's Surveyor of Taxes Office and pays property taxes to the Province, not to the FVRD or the City of Mission. Under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act, s.11, rural property taxes are due and payable on July 2 of the year they are first levied, a 5% penalty is added to any portion that remains unpaid on July 2, and a further 5% penalty is added to any portion that remains unpaid on October 31. The City of Mission's flat 10% penalty after July 2 does NOT apply here — tax follows the jurisdiction (FVRD Electoral Area G / rural provincial), not the Mission mailing address.

items.t: The mailing address is the trap. Every listing here carries a Mission address, the page title says "Mission BC," and the editorial heading calls this "Mission's Rural Frontier" — and none of it governs anything. The FVRD is the local government, the Province collects the tax, and Mission's bylaws, OCP and flat 10% tax penalty stop at the city boundary.
The tax penalty calendar is split, not flat.

The Deroche Bench crosses an electoral-area line. The eastern portions of the Deroche Bench sit in Electoral Area C, not Area G — two otherwise similar bench parcels can answer to different FVRD plan areas, and which side of the G/C line a specific parcel sits on is UNVERIFIED at parcel level. Check the electoral area for the PID, not the community name.

"Area G" is not a unique bylaw address. At least two other BC regional districts (Nanaimo; Okanagan-Similkameen) also have an Electoral Area G with its own OCP bylaws — a web search for "Area G OCP bylaw" returns those districts' numbers, which have nothing to do with Dewdney or Deroche.
One park, two products. An age label for this corridor is read off the park's own rules, in writing.

Water is a service-area question, not a community question. Both Dewdney and Deroche have FVRD community water systems on the FVRD's own bylaw record — and lots outside the service areas are on wells. "Deroche has community water" is true and useless; the parcel's service-area position is the fact that matters.

items.t: Jurisdiction — FVRD Electoral Area G (stated expressly): the FVRD is the local government for this unincorporated ground. City of Mission bylaws (including OCP Bylaw 6405-2026 and Zoning Bylaw 5949-2020), Mission suite rules and Mission tax dates do NOT apply here and are never borrowed.

Planning/zoning process — numbers UNVERIFIED, process documented: 0866, 2009) is a guide-only claim, not adopted as verified. Other regional districts' Area G bylaws (e.g., Nanaimo, Okanagan-Similkameen) are a name collision, NOT citable for FVRD Area G. The process instead: confirm the parcel's plan designation and zone with the FVRD for the PID before relying on any use, suite or subdivision claim.

Property taxes — RURAL regime (stated expressly): a property not located in a city, town, district or village is in a rural area; its owner receives the tax notice from the Province's Surveyor of Taxes Office and pays the Province, not the FVRD or the City of Mission. Under the Taxation (Rural Area) Act, s.11, rural taxes are due July 2, a 5% penalty is added to any portion unpaid on July 2, and a further 5% to any portion unpaid on October 31. The City of Mission flat 10% penalty does NOT apply to this ground.
Pad tenure, where met (manufactured homes on rented pads in the feed): a manufactured home on a rented pad is NOT lot stock / NOT land ownership.

blocks.text: Good to know about Dewdney Deroche

items.t: The Area C line at the east end (Nov 1, 2026). The FVRD's Electoral Area C plan area begins east of Deroche and includes the eastern portions of the Deroche Bench — so two neighbouring Bench parcels can sit in different electoral areas with different FVRD plans. Which side of the G/C line a specific parcel sits on is UNVERIFIED at parcel level; check the PID before quoting any plan rule.

Floodplain is the corridor's standing condition (2022 freshet record, read Nov 1, 2026). FVRD freshet alerts have covered Nicomen Island and the Taylor Road area in Deroche, and Dewdney Regional Park is listed among flood-related park closures — lowland pricing that ignores dyke and flood-construction diligence is mispricing.

Guide-only claims (the Area G census figures, Dewdney Regional Park address/hours, Inch Creek Hatchery details, Dewdney Area Improvement District figures, the Area G OCP Bylaw No. 0866 citation, the Hatzic Middle catchment assertion, and the Mission Senior Secondary replacement funding figures) are UNVERIFIED site copy, not defects and not facts.

faq.q: Who do I pay property tax to on a Dewdney or Deroche property?
faq.a: The Province: rural-area properties receive their tax notice from the Surveyor of Taxes Office and pay the Province, not the FVRD or a municipality; rural taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty on amounts unpaid on July 2 and a further 5% on amounts unpaid on October 31.

faq.q: Can I build a second home on an acreage here?
faq.a: It depends on the parcel's FVRD zoning and, for farmland, the ALR: ALR parcels are limited to one principal residence of at most 500 m² plus at most one additional residence of 90 m² (parcels ≤40 ha) or 186 m² (parcels >40 ha), and non-ALR lots follow the FVRD zoning bylaw for the parcel — confirm both for the specific PID before relying on a second-dwelling plan.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Dewdney-Deroche?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 2 houses listed with 0 sold in the month in Dewdney-Deroche. Those are month-end counts and move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Are there any condos in Dewdney-Deroche?
faq.a: None verified — no condo building in this corridor was confirmed on an official, developer or strata source in the research, and no townhome complex was confirmed either. The verified stock is manufactured homes in parks, detached houses and acreages. A buyer who wants a Fraser Valley condo is buying in Mission city or Chilliwack, documented in those areas' condo notes — not in this corridor.

faq.q: Are Dewdney and Deroche part of Mission?
faq.a: No. Listings carry Mission mailing addresses, but Dewdney and Deroche are unincorporated FVRD Electoral Area G communities — the FVRD's housing-needs report lists Area G as "Nicomen Island, Deroche, Dewdney, Hatzic Island" — and the City of Mission does not govern them.
